Which of the following is the best upper bound for the length of $\overset{―}{BC},$ obtained using the triangle inequality theorem only?

(*Note: Figure not drawn to scale*)
question.worked_solution:
The triangle inequality theorem states that the length of any one side must be smaller than the sum of the other two sides.

- Applying the triangle inequality theorem to $△BAC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & <BA+AC \\ BC & <8\,\text{cm}+3\,\text{cm} \\ BC & <11\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Applying the triangle inequality theorem to $△BDC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & <BD+DC \\ BC & <4\,\text{cm}+9\,\text{cm} \\ BC & <13\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since both $BC<11\,\text{cm}$ and $BC<13\,\text{cm}$ must be satisfied, we conclude that 

$$
BC<11\,\text{cm}.
$$
